claims.text: The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr RHEA has a single-phase BCC structure.
The baseline alloy has a density of approximately 13–14 g/cm³.
The baseline alloy fractures brittly at room temperature with less than 5% compressive strain.
Adding 0.5–2.0 at.% Si or B and applying the specified solutionizing and aging treatment will precipitate coherent (Hf,Zr)2Si, (Hf,Zr)2B, or B2-type intermetallics.
The precipitates will form a reticulated network of coherent 10–50 nm particles within a continuous BCC matrix.
The proposed (Hf,Zr)2Si or (Hf,Zr)2B Laves-type phases will be ductile and coherent.
A brittle HCP phase is present in or observed for the baseline alloy.
Coherent precipitates impede dislocation motion and thereby provide precipitation hardening.
Low-misfit coherent interfaces allow precipitate shearing or Orowan bypass without producing crack-initiating stress concentrations.
A continuous disordered BCC matrix promotes plasticity relative to a continuous ordered B2 matrix.
A reticulated precipitate network will deflect and blunt propagating cracks.
The intervention will increase compressive yield strength by 40–60%, from approximately 1500 MPa to 2200–2400 MPa.
The modified alloy will achieve a room-temperature compressive fracture strain greater than 15%.
Si or B addition will slightly decrease the density or leave it approximately unchanged.
High-volume-fraction ceramic reinforcement can increase compressive strength while retaining cleavage fracture and negligible room-temperature ductility.
An intermetallic volume fraction above 15 vol.% will produce brittle behavior.
A precipitate-to-matrix lattice misfit above approximately 2% will make the precipitates crack-initiation sites.
The proposed operating regime is room-temperature uniaxial compression at a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1.
The mechanism is falsified for this system if coherent precipitates are present but the alloy still remains brittle.
The thermodynamic stability and aging-temperature window for coherent (Hf,Zr)2Si or (Hf,Zr)2B precipitation in this quinary alloy are uncertain.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis refers to a brittle HCP phase observed in the baseline, whereas the initial-state and baseline fields define that alloy as single-phase BCC with no secondary phase.

The density trade-off is described both as a slight decrease or negligible change for Si/B addition and as a possible slight increase for heavier additions, although the proposed additions are only Si or B.
